audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for greatness, child/little ones, stumbling-blocks, lost sheep, community restoration process, binding/loosing, agreement prayer, seventy-seven forgiveness, and unforgiving servant parable.

verses.restored: At that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, Who then is greatest in the reign of the heavens?

familiar.text: At the same time came the disciples unto Jesus, saying, Who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?

verses.restored: Calling a child, he stood the child in their midst

familiar.text: And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them,

verses.restored: and said, Amen, I say to you: unless you turn and become like children, you will certainly not enter the reign of the heavens.

familiar.text: And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.

verses.restored: Therefore whoever humbles himself like this child, this one is greatest in the reign of the heavens.

familiar.text: Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.

verses.restored: Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me.

familiar.text: And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.

verses.restored: But whoever causes one of these little ones trusting in me to stumble, it would be better for him that a large millstone be hung around his neck and he be sunk in the depth of the sea.

familiar.text: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.

verses.restored: Woe to the world because of stumbling-blocks; for stumbling-blocks must come, yet woe to the person through whom the stumbling-block comes.

familiar.text: Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh!

verses.restored: If your hand or foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it from you; it is better to enter life maimed or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the age-long fire.

familiar.text: Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire.

verses.restored: If your eye causes you to stumble, remove it and throw it from you; it is better to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the Gehenna of fire.

familiar.text: And if thine eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life with one eye, rather than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire.

verses.restored: See that you do not despise one of these little ones; for I say to you that their messengers in the heavens continually see the face of my Father in the heavens.

familiar.text: Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add: For the Son of Humanity came to save the lost.]

familiar.text: For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.

verses.restored: What do you think? If a person has a hundred sheep and one of them wanders, does he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go seek the wandering one?

familiar.text: How think ye? if a man have an hundred sheep, and one of them be gone astray, doth he not leave the ninety and nine, and goeth into the mountains, and seeketh that which is gone astray?

verses.restored: If he finds it, amen, I say to you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not wander.

familiar.text: And if so be that he find it, verily I say unto you, he rejoiceth more of that sheep, than of the ninety and nine which went not astray.

verses.restored: In the same way, it is not the will before your Father in the heavens that one of these little ones should be lost.

familiar.text: Even so it is not the will of your Father which is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish.

verses.restored: If your brother or sister sins/misaligns, go and show the fault between you and that one alone; if that one hears you, you have gained your brother or sister.

familiar.text: Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.

verses.restored: But if that one does not hear, take with you one or two more, so that by the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.

familiar.text: But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.

verses.restored: If that one refuses to hear them, tell it to the assembly; and if that one refuses to hear even the assembly, let that one be to you as the Gentile and the tax collector.

familiar.text: And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: whatever you bind on earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will have been loosed in heaven.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.

verses.restored: Again, amen, I say to you: if two of you agree on earth about any matter they ask, it will come to be for them from my Father in the heavens.

familiar.text: Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven.

verses.restored: For where two or three are gathered into my name, there I am in their midst.

familiar.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.

verses.restored: Then Peter came and said to him, Lord, how often will my brother or sister sin/misalign against me and I release them? Up to seven times?

familiar.text: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?

verses.restored: Jesus said to him, I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy-seven times.

familiar.text: Jesus saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.

verses.restored: Because of this, the reign of the heavens is like a human king who wanted to settle accounts with his servants.

familiar.text: Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account of his servants.

verses.restored: As he began to settle, one debtor of ten thousand talents was brought to him.

familiar.text: And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, which owed him ten thousand talents.

verses.restored: Since he did not have enough to repay, the lord commanded him to be sold, with wife and children and all he had, and repayment to be made.

familiar.text: But forasmuch as he had not to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made.

verses.restored: The servant fell down and bowed before him, saying, Be patient with me, and I will repay you everything.

familiar.text: The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

verses.restored: Moved with compassion, the lord of that servant released him and forgave/released the debt.

familiar.text: Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt.

verses.restored: But that servant went out and found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred denarii; seizing him, he began to choke him, saying, Repay what you owe.

familiar.text: But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellowservants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest.

verses.restored: His fellow servant fell down and begged him, saying, Be patient with me, and I will repay you.

familiar.text: And his fellowservant fell down at his feet, and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all.

verses.restored: But he was not willing; instead he went and threw him into prison until he should repay the debt.

familiar.text: And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt.

verses.restored: When his fellow servants saw what had happened, they were deeply grieved and came and explained to their lord all that had happened.

familiar.text: So when his fellowservants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done.

verses.restored: Then his lord called him and said, Harmful servant, I forgave/released you all that debt because you begged me.

familiar.text: Then his lord, after that he had called him, said unto him, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me:

verses.restored: Was it not necessary for you also to have mercy on your fellow servant, as I had mercy on you?

familiar.text: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee?

verses.restored: In anger his lord handed him to the jailers until he should repay all that was owed.

familiar.text: And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due unto him.

verses.restored: So also my heavenly Father will do to you if each of you does not release your brother or sister from your hearts.

familiar.text: So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.
